items.title: Admit Astral Rust machinery as the static Python evidence plane
items.summary: Astral's Ruff/ty workspace already provides Rust parser, AST, incremental database/index, semantic, module-resolution and type-analysis machinery. ctrl should consume and correlate these observations instead of recreating solved static-analysis infrastructure, while retaining CPython as the compiler/runtime semantic authority.
items.localContractImpact: Add an Astral analyzer adapter family to the future CPython control/python-intel implementation; map analyzer observations into the same typed evidence graph and dispatch CPython probes for material static/dynamic disagreements.

observations.observation: astral-sh/ruff@a9663e243a571b4aed032ee243da25189d2bc95b contains the Rust parser/AST/index/semantic crates and the ty resolver/core/semantic/IDE crates required for a reusable static Python analysis substrate.

ty_python_semantic depends on ruff_db, Salsa-enabled ruff_index, ruff_python_ast, ruff_python_parser, ty_module_resolver, ty_site_packages, ty_python_core and ty_static, establishing an explicit reusable Rust dependency graph.
ruff_python_semantic separately consumes Ruff AST/parser/index infrastructure, so Ruff lint semantics and ty type semantics remain distinct analyzer observations over shared machinery.

CPython 3.14 compiler evidence remains the authority for lexical/compiler behavior; Astral results are correlated analyzer observations and disagreement triggers probes rather than authority promotion.

claims.text: ctrl should reuse Astral's Rust static-analysis substrate rather than implement another Python parser/index/resolver/type engine.
Astral analyzer observations remain evidence-only; contradictory CPython compiler/runtime evidence is preserved and takes semantic precedence for CPython behavior.

items.title: Keep Astral main separate from ctrl's lock-selected analyzer baseline
items.summary: The monitor watches astral-sh/ruff@main as forecast evidence. The actually realized Ruff/ty versions used by ctrl remain selected by ctrl's uv.lock and must be resolved separately before analyzer output can qualify a concrete ctrl revision.
items.localContractImpact: Future analyzer execution should record both uv.lock package identity and Astral source/release provenance instead of treating main as the installed baseline.
